4.0.0.en: “And in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying, We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name, to take away our reproach.” [1].

4.0.1.en: These seven women are all the nations, among them the Jews, for all felt an extreme emptiness invading the depths because of the corruption of human nature. These nations gather as a bride seeking her Bridegroom; she wants His name that He may take away the reproach of her corruption, and then she eats her own bread and wears her own apparel. Her Christ is more important than all her needs; in Him she finds all satisfaction, covering from nakedness and protection from all shame.

4.0.2.en: This is from the symbolic, spiritual side. As for the literal side, the prophet Isaiah prophesied what would befall Judah, as it would be exposed to fierce wars in which a great number of men would be killed, so that every woman would long to find a man for herself under whose name she might take shelter, whatever it cost her. She is ready to share him with six other women, which is something a woman by her nature cannot bear; she even asks her husband not to be obliged to provide anything, but she eats and drinks from her own labor, which is contrary to nature itself... All this is because she wants to bear children by him, so that her reproach may be taken away (Gen 30:23; 1 Sam 1:11).

4.1.0.en: 2 In that day shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel.

4.1.1.en: Now, if humanity with all its peoples (the seven women) has discovered its need for the Savior, here the prophet announces to it His coming, saying: “In that day shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel” [2].

4.1.2.en: “That day” means the fullness of time (Gal 4:4), in which the Only-Begotten Son of God became incarnate, who was called “the Branch of the LORD,” or “the Branch” (Jer 23:5; 33:15; Zech 3:8; 6:12). He is the Branch of the LORD and a Branch of righteousness for David, for He is the One born before all ages, eternally, of the very essence of the Father, and by His Incarnation He was born of the seed of David.

4.1.3.en: By His entry into the world He declared the divine splendor and the surpassing glory upon the simple strangers who believe, as well as upon those of the Jews who are saved. As Simeon the elder said: “A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.”

4.1.4.en: This Branch sprouted by His Incarnation, and dwelt in our midst to reflect the divine splendor upon our nature, so He says to His Church: “Thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD” (Ezek 16:14).

4.1.5.en: The word “branch” also corresponds to “Nazareth,” so the Evangelist says: “That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene” (Mt 2:23).

4.2.0.en: 3 And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem: 4 When the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning, who is it that enjoys the Branch of the LORD?

4.2.1.en: “He that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem” [3]. These are the few who accepted faith in the Lord Christ from among the community of the Jews; they remained in the spiritual Zion, in the Church, the new Jerusalem.

4.2.2.en: From the literal side it refers to the remnant that remained from the captivity, but from the spiritual side it is the holy few, the little flock whose heart does not leave Zion and whose spirit does not depart from the Jerusalem above. Many of the prophets spoke of this remnant (Zech 13:9), and it has been found in every age: in the days of Elijah the prophet the Lord declared that He had seven thousand men who had not bowed the knee to Baal; during the captivity Daniel was found with the three young men among the holy few, and also Esther and Mordecai; and after the captivity we also hear of this holy few (Mal 3:6; 4:2); and the Lord Christ Himself speaks of the little flock to whom it is the Father's good pleasure to give the Kingdom (Lk 12).

4.2.3.en: In brief, every faithful soul that lifts its heart to the Jerusalem above sees the Church, holy in the Lord, and rejoices and is glad because of her.

4.2.4.en: Isaiah's heart was bound to Jerusalem, the capital of his country and the city of God which contains His holy temple, and he entered into bitterness because of the corruption that had come upon it. Now, as he announces the coming of “the Branch of the LORD,” he sees a new Jerusalem inhabited by saints in the holy Lord, who enjoy eternal life. He says: “Shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem” [3].

4.2.5.en: The Church, the icon of heaven, is the pledge of the Jerusalem above, into which nothing defiled or unclean may enter, nor anyone who makes a lie, but only he who has washed his robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb (Rev 7:14).

4.2.6.en: As members of the holy Church, the new Jerusalem, we have enjoyed the anointing of the Spirit of the Holy God, that we may fulfill the evangelical commandment: “But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation” (1 Pet 1:15).

4.3.0.en: Who sanctifies our life? The Lord Himself, for the prophet says: “When the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughter of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning” [4]. He washed our defilements in the waters of Baptism by the merits of His blood, and He still washes all our weaknesses with His blood that flowed from His pierced side mingled with water. If our hands have been stained with blood through our sins, He offers His blood as an atonement for us, to present us as a glorious Church, not having spot or wrinkle, but holy in everything.

4.3.1.en: This washing or purging is accomplished “by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.” The spirit of judgment was accomplished by His being lifted up on the Cross, bearing the price of our sins in His body, fulfilling divine justice on our behalf in Himself. As for the spirit of burning, it means what the Law had previously announced in the Book of Leviticus concerning the “burnt offering,” where the sacrifice is burned completely as a sign of perfect love... So the sacrifice of Christ in our name is the “burnt offering” that was offered as a sign of our perfect love in Him toward the Father. Perhaps by the spirit of burning he also meant the fiery Holy Spirit who descended upon the Church to sanctify her and wash every member in her.

4.3.2.en: * In the last days, when the fullness of the time of freedom came, the Word Himself washed the filth of the daughter of Zion, for He washed the feet of the disciples with His own hands (Jn 13:5).

4.3.3.en: St. Irenaeus * The excellent spiritual bath (of Baptism) removes the corruption of the soul.

4.3.4.en: St. Clement of Alexandria St. Clement of Alexandria comments on the saying “purged the blood of Jerusalem” by saying: [Here is the blood of the crime and the killing of the prophets]; for whoever denied Christ shared with his fathers in the killing of the prophets, but whoever received Him has been purified and sanctified in his depths.

4.4.s.en: 4. Christ's dwelling in the midst of His Church:

4.4.0.en: 5 And the LORD will create upon every dwelling place of mount Zion, and upon her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory shall be a defence.

4.4.1.en: The Church is washed by the spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning, that is, through the unique burnt sacrifice that the Lord Christ offered and by the work of the Holy Spirit in the waters of Baptism, and so she asks for the dwelling of her slain Bridegroom in her midst; He covers her by day like a cloud that shades them and leads her by night as a pillar of smoke and a pillar of fire that lights the way for her. Thus the Church recalls in her memory the tabernacle of meeting in the midst of the wilderness, where God met with His people, but it is a new tabernacle on a level different from the tabernacle of the Old Covenant, in that:

4.4.2.en: A. “Upon every dwelling place” [5]: the divine presence or divine indwelling is no longer limited to a tent or a temple, but He dwells in His Church, which extends everywhere, in the east and in the west; He dwells in the hearts of the priests and the people, and His doors are open to all peoples and nations wherever they are.

4.4.3.en: B. “And upon her assemblies”: this expression points to God's work in the Church as one assembly, or one community, in which each member enjoys the gift of the divine indwelling not as an isolated individual but as a living member of the community, joined with the rest of the members through Christ the Head; he has his personal relationship with God, which increases his union with his brethren.

4.4.4.en: C. “Will create... a cloud and smoke and the shining of a flaming fire”: the Lord Christ is the secret of the protection and illumination of His Church.

4.4.5.en: D. His saying: “For upon all the glory shall be a defence” means that the glory of the king's daughter is within (Ps 45), hidden in her. Outwardly she shares with her Christ His sufferings, His crucifixion, His death and His burial, so that what was said of her Bridegroom is said of her: “He hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him” (Isa 53:2); and inwardly she shares with Him the glory of His Resurrection.

4.4.6.en: The soul that realizes the value of the inner glory of its Christ and the joy of His Kingdom within it covers it because it is precious... For we are accustomed to hide what is precious and keep it, while what is worthless needs no covering or keeping. The Church, in her preoccupation with her glorified Christ, says: “He shall lie all night betwixt my breasts” (Song 1:13)... She wants Him in her depths, hidden in her heart!

4.5.s.en: 5. The Church of Christ as a tabernacle and a refuge:

4.5.0.en: 6 And there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain.

4.5.1.en: The Lord dwells in His Church and makes of her a tabernacle that shields the suffering, wounded souls from the heat of the day, and shelters them from storms and rains (Isa 4:6).

4.5.2.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that this tabernacle is the great cloud of witnesses (Heb 12:1), saying: [The remembrance of the saints raises up and restores the soul that has been weighed down with woes, so that it becomes like a cloud that protects it from the very hot and burning rays (of the sun).]

5.0.0.en: “Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill: and he fenced it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and planted it with the choicest vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and also made a winepress therein: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes” [1-2].

5.0.1.en: This song proclaims the story of divine love, in which God loved man and still loves him and cares for him, and God continues in His love while man meets love with barrenness. This story was fulfilled with our first parents Adam and Eve, and also with the people of God at the beginning of their existence, for Moses the prophet says: “For the LORD's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance. He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he compassed him about, he watched him, he kept him as the apple of his eye” (Deut 32:9-10). God brought His people out of bondage not merely to give them the land flowing with milk and honey, but to establish the Church of the New Testament that fills the whole earth and enjoys the inner Kingdom of God, as the psalmist says: “Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it. Thou preparedst room before it, and didst cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land” (Ps 80:8-9).

5.0.2.en: It is clear that the “vineyard” here refers to the whole people: the kingdom of Israel and Judah; so what did the Lord present to His beloved people?

5.0.3.en: A. He set them on “a very fruitful hill” [1], for He brought them into Canaan, which flows with milk and honey; so the drought that comes and the famines that occur are not due to the nature of the land or the circumstances of the region, but are the fruit of the sins of the people.

5.0.4.en: God established the Church of the New Testament on a fruitful hill, for He lifted her heart as if to heaven, that her children might enjoy the richness of the heavenly life, so that they are satisfied and lack nothing.

5.1.0.en: B. “He fenced it (made a hedge around it)” [2]: this hedge is the Law with which the Lord surrounded His people anciently, so that they would not mingle with the surrounding pagan nations and take over their abominations from them. As St. John Chrysostom says: [The Law is a hedge, made for safety (Isa 8:20)]. St. Ambrose sees that the wall is “the divine providence that keeps the vineyard from the attack of the spiritual beast.” And St. Jerome sees that it is the guarding of the angels.

5.1.1.en: C. “And gathered out the stones thereof” [2]: the stones refer to pagan worship, where the idols were of stone, which the Lord removed from the midst of His people, or removed His people from them, so that all might live a godly life. The stones also refer to the nature of hardness and violence which our Lord Jesus wants to remove from every heart by the work of His Holy Spirit. In the words of Ezekiel the prophet: “I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh” (Ezek 11:9). This new heart and new spirit (Ezek 36:26) is realized by our receiving the new spiritual birth in the waters of holy Baptism. St. Cyprian says: [It is Baptism in which the old man dies and the new man is born, as the Apostle declares, affirming that He saved us by the washing of regeneration (Titus 3:5).]

5.1.2.en: D. “Planted it with the choicest vine (a chosen vine)” [2], that is, He planted it as a vine of the best kinds of vines, as a chosen people that received a covenant with God, that it might bear “truth” in it, as the Lord says: “Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” (Jer 2:21).

5.1.3.en: As for the Church of the New Testament, “the Truth” Himself came, the Word of God incarnate, to present Himself as a vine who carries us in Him as living branches that bring forth much fruit (Jn 15:5).

5.1.4.en: E. “And built a tower in the midst of it” [2], in which the owner of the vineyard or the watchman dwells to guard the vineyard from the attacks of thieves and wild beasts. Some scholars see that the tower is the company of the prophets and priests and all the spiritual and civil leaders who ought to have watched over the flock and kept it from the little foxes that spoil the vines.

5.1.5.en: In the New Testament the tower is the altar of the Lord that is set up within the soul, on which the believer offers his prayers, his fasts, his gifts and his whole life as a burnt offering to the Lord, through his union with the sacrificed Christ. Through this spiritual tower the Church of Christ is kept strong and effective in every heart, where the believers enjoy fellowship and union with the Lord Himself.

5.1.6.en: F. “And also made a winepress therein” [2], for pressing the grapes and making the wine of love that is offered for spiritual joy. What is this winepress but the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, who trod the winepress alone, and of the nations there was none with Him (Isa 63:3). He offered His blood, poured out, as the wine of love that gladdens every believing heart.

5.1.7.en: St. Ambrose says: [He dug a winepress, because the mysteries of the sufferings of Christ appear like new wine... and the crowd supposed that the disciples were drunk when they received the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:13). He dug the vat of a winepress so that the inner fruit might be poured out in it.]

5.1.8.en: St. Irenaeus says: [God planted the vineyard of the human race when He first created Adam and chose the fathers, then He committed it into the hands of the vinedressers when He established the Mosaic dispensation, and He fenced it by presenting teachings concerning their worship of Him, and built a tower by choosing Jerusalem, and dug a winepress when He prepared a vessel for the prophetic Spirit. And so He sent prophets before the Babylonian captivity, and then more prophets (during the captivity and after it), seeking the fruits...]

5.1.9.en: What did the vineyard give to its owner?

5.1.10.en: “And he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes” [2]. The Lord expected to gather love in return for love, and repentance and remorse in return for the forgiveness of His sins, but He found hardened hearts that bring forth no fruits worthy of repentance. All have gone astray and become corrupt and come short of the glory of God, so it was fitting for the Word of God to come down to us as a new vine, who alone plants us in Him so that we bring forth much fruit (Jn 15:5).

5.1.11.en: * When He says: “I am the true vine” (Jn 15:1), He distinguishes Himself without doubt from that one to whom He addressed the words: “How then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” (Jer 2:21), for how could a true vine, from which it is expected to bring forth grapes, have brought forth thorns?!

5.1.12.en: * I expected it to bring forth fruit, and I found sin.

5.1.13.en: St. Augustine * I longed for it (the vine) to give wine, and it brought forth thorns. Behold, you see the crown with which I am adorned.

5.2.s.en: 2. A judgment between God and His people:

5.2.0.en: 3 And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard. 4 What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes? 5 And now go to; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; and break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down: 6 And I will lay it waste: it shall not be pruned, nor digged; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it. 7 For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for truth, but behold bloodshed; for justice, but behold a cry.

5.3.0.en: Nothing is harder than for a being to enter into a judgment with a son who is beloved to him, but before the hardness of man's heart and his ingratitude He asked to stand before His people for a dialogue, asking: “What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it?!” [4]. And the wonder is that He left the judgment to the other party, to His opponents, so that they might judge themselves by themselves. This is God's way in dealing with us: He exposes our souls before us, and uncovers our weaknesses before our eyes, and leaves us to judge ourselves by ourselves, not because He wants to win or to punish, but because He seeks our return to Him and our entering into relations of love and affection with Him.

5.3.1.en: What more could God have done with us than He did?! He created us out of nothing, and set us in His image and likeness, and gave us the earth with what is on it and under it and above it, and offered the stars for our benefit, and when our nature became corrupt He sent us His Law and His prophets, and finally He came Himself to write the song of His love in blood in His body on the Cross!

5.3.2.en: Since the vineyard found nothing with which to answer the Vinedresser, wonderful in His love, the Vinedresser began to announce His disciplines so that the vineyard might be moved, which are:

5.4.0.en: A. “I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up” [5]. If the angel of the Lord encamps round about them that fear Him (Ps 34:7), and the Lord Himself is a wall of fire round about His people (Zech 2:5), then God in His love gives up the opponents and removes from them the heavenly guard, that they may realize their weakness and feel that they are without hedge or wall, so that wild beasts enter among them to graze as in a desert or a bare wilderness, perhaps that they may return to God and seek Him as a refuge for themselves.

5.4.1.en: If the grace of God is removed from a person, he becomes without a hedge, and his soul opens to the love of the world, so that its herds of unclean swine enter and go out without hindrance, and his heart becomes trodden down by unclean lusts and his thoughts wander in abominations, and his senses descend into evil desire.

5.4.2.en: As St. Clement of Alexandria says: [These things (the removal of the hedge and the permission for enemies to enter) are accomplished by divine permission to turn them to good and edification. For [divine providence is an art of discipline.]

5.5.0.en: B. “I will lay it waste: it shall not be pruned, nor digged” [6]. When the Lord departs from His vineyard, that is, the human soul, it comes to be in emptiness and is counted a waste. The Lord weeps over it as He wept over Jerusalem, saying: “Behold, your house is left unto you desolate” (Mt 23:38).

5.5.1.en: When the vineyard bears fruit, the vinedresser prunes and digs it so that it may bring forth greater fruit, but if it brings forth wild grapes he does not stretch out his hand to it. If the pruning and digging point to the Lord's tender disciplines toward His children, then as we walk with Him in the way, He stretches out His hand to us as His children, caring for us and tending us and also disciplining us so that we increase in the fruit of the Spirit. So not pruning and not digging point to the absence of discipline, and this is the harshest kind of punishment... total neglect and being unworthy even of discipline. As St. John Chrysostom says: [When the physician stops giving the bitter medicine or using the scalpel, this means that the patient's condition is completely hopeless.

5.5.2.en: C. “But there shall come up briers and thorns” [6]. This is the fruit of man's withdrawing from God and separating from Him, for he brings forth from himself thorns and briers. The Apostle says: “And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient” (Rom 2:28).

5.5.3.en: What is this thorn but man's losing his peace, to carry within him troubles and cares that he cannot face by himself alone?!

5.5.4.en: D. “I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it” [6]. Rain in the Old Testament points to the gift of the Holy Spirit, for the man who is ungrateful to the Lord and seeks separation from Him loses the indwelling of the Spirit in him, and his heart turns into a wilderness that bears no fruit of the Spirit. Therefore instead of bringing forth “truth” he brings forth “bloodshed,” and instead of “justice” he brings forth “a cry” [7].

5.6.0.en: The Lord seeks to find in us His garden, fruitful by the Spirit, where the soul speaks to Him, saying: “Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits” [16]. But the soul's deprivation of the spiritual rain turns the delightful garden into a dreadful place in which there is nothing but bloodshed and continual crying!

5.6.1.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that rain in the Holy Bible points to teaching. Thus when a person denies God he deprives himself of enjoying the Lord's teaching in his depths; he reads the word of God and perhaps studies it, but he does not enjoy its efficacy and sweetness in his depths. This is what St. Augustine declared in his first homily on the Gospel according to our teacher Matthew the Evangelist, saying: [He was like a little bird in a nest, who in the pride of his heart wanted to fly by himself, studying the Holy Bible in a spirit of criticism, and fell to the ground, and the passers-by almost crushed him under their feet, had it not been for the grace of God which snatched him up and returned him to the nest of faith until he had two wings with which he can fly.

5.6.2.en: St. Augustine sees that the rain here points to the preaching that passed from the vineyard (the Jewish people) to the Gentiles.

5.6.3.en: He says: “For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for truth, but behold bloodshed; for justice, but behold a cry” [7].

5.6.4.en: God gave every possibility to the whole community: to the priests and Levites as to the people, to the rich as to the poor, to the learned as to the unlearned, that this vineyard might bring forth “truth” and “justice,” and “the Truth” came incarnate from the tribe of Judah, but they shed His blood, and instead of justice there was the cry: “Crucify Him, crucify Him.”

5.7.s.en: 3. A detailed presentation of the sins of Israel:

5.7.0.en: 8 Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth! 9 In mine ears said the LORD of hosts, Of a truth many houses shall be desolate, even great and fair, without inhabitant. 10 Yea, ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and the seed of an homer shall yield an ephah. 11 Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them! 12 And the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts: but they regard not the work of the LORD, neither consider the operation of his hands. 13 Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge: and their honourable men are famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst. 14 Therefore hell hath enlarged herself, and opened her mouth without measure: and their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that rejoiceth, shall descend into it. 15 And the mean man shall be brought down, and the mighty man shall be humbled, and the eyes of the lofty shall be humbled: 16 But the LORD of hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and God that is holy shall be sanctified in righteousness. 17 Then shall the lambs feed after their manner, and the waste places of the fat ones shall strangers eat. 18 Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope: 19 That say, Let him make speed, and hasten his work, that we may see it: and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw nigh and come, that we may know it! 20 Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter! 21 Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight! 22 Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink: 23 Which justify the wicked for reward, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!

5.7.1.en: After the Lord disclosed His love for His vineyard and His surpassing care for it, and how the vineyard deprived itself of the sweet spiritual fruit or the gladdening wine, and made thorns that were woven into a crown upon the head of the Lord Christ, He began to review the most important sins of the people and their evil fruit, which brought bitter woes instead of enjoying the blessings of the Lord and the fellowship of His glories.

5.7.2.en: A. “Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!” [8]. By this he means that they were absorbed in buying houses and fields by every means, in selfishness, until one did not leave a place for his brother, especially the poor and needy. A very small few owned the agricultural land and the houses in order to exploit the common people, and this contrary to the Law, which required that the lands remain distributed equally (Num 33:54) and that in the year of Jubilee everyone's property return to him (Lev 25).

5.7.3.en: The land in Canaan is a free gift presented to the whole people so that all might live in prosperity, enjoying what it pours forth of milk and honey, as though it were the property of the Lord who gives it to them. But by these actions they committed the sin of greed and also of pride, with disobedience and the breaking of the Law. Therefore the blessing was removed and the curse came, so the houses become desolate because of death or captivity; in a moment 185,000 died in the war. Moreover, the fields do not bear fruit as usual, for ten acres of vineyard yield one bath (about 27.5 kilograms) instead of about 500 baths; and an homer (283.5 kilograms) of seed yields an ephah [a tenth of a homer (Ezek 45:11)], that is, the harvest amounts to a tenth of the seed that was cast into the ground.

5.8.0.en: B. “Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them!” [11]. If the first woe fell on them because of greed and injustice, the second is because of excessive frivolity. They came to be drunk in the early morning instead of rising for work, and they also stay until a late hour of the night, that is, they are drunk by day and by night. Thus they break the divine commandments: “Man goeth forth unto his work and to his labour until the evening” (Ps 104:23). Their life turned from the spiritual joy mixed with the seriousness of life and worship into a frivolity mixed with laxity; they use all the instruments of music [12] while being occupied with holding feasts to excite their feelings and senses to evil, ignoring the godly life in the Lord. As Amos the prophet says: “That chant to the sound of the viol, and invent to themselves instruments of musick, like David; that drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph. Therefore now shall they go captive with the first that go captive, and the banquet of them that stretched themselves shall be removed” (Amos 6:6-7).

5.8.1.en: * See how God blames luxury also; for He does not condemn them here for a greed they committed but merely for extravagance. Behold, you eat to excess while Christ has not what is necessary. You eat various cakes while Christ has not dry bread. You drink Thasian wine and do not give Christ a cup of cold water, though He is thirsty. You lie on a soft embroidered bed while He perishes from cold.

5.9.0.en: St. John Chrysostom As for the work of frivolity, it is the captivity of the inner man away from the knowledge of the truth, to live a captive of ignorance, hungering and thirsting inwardly, with nothing to satisfy or quench him. The prophet says: “Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge: and their honourable men are famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst” [13]. The wise man says: “For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags” (Prov 13:21).

5.10.0.en: Through frivolity a person loses his inner awareness and descends to the abyss, which opens its doors wide to swallow without limit. In this a person loses his splendor and his joy [14], and falls into humiliation [15].

5.10.1.en: This is the bitter fruit gathered by those who walk in the wide gate, the gate of continual frivolity to satisfy temporal lusts. But what is more serious is their eternal destruction, for he says: “Therefore hell hath enlarged herself, and opened her mouth without measure: and their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that rejoiceth, shall descend into it” [14]. He portrays the abyss, Sheol, like an opening of the earth to swallow the wicked, as happened with Korah and his company... It opens to ask for more, swallowing them into the depths so that they remain in darkness forever.

5.11.0.en: This is what happens to those occupied with a life of luxury and frivolity; but as for God, the LORD of hosts, He is exalted and sanctified by His condemnation of sin in justice and righteousness [16].

5.12.0.en: Perhaps some will ask: What is the state of the faithful little remnant of the Lord? The prophet answers: “Then shall the lambs feed after their manner, and the waste places of the fat ones shall strangers eat” [17]. The sheep, the little flock, graze wherever the Good Shepherd, Jesus Christ, leads them, for He keeps them from injustice and persecution. These eat in quiet and safety without anyone disturbing them (Ex 34:14). When the Church of the Old Testament is laid waste by the Jews' refusal of faith in the Lord Christ, the Gentiles (the strangers) inherit the promises, the covenants, the Law, the prophecies and so on...

5.13.0.en: C. “Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope!” [18]. This third woe falls on those who seek sin with intense desire and diligence; they strive for it of their own choice and push themselves to it or pull it forcefully toward them. Danger comes upon these, for they fall into the cords of vanity and are tied to the cart of sin so as to become attached to it.

5.13.1.en: They draw sin as with a rope, and since it is extremely heavy it collapses upon their heads and shatters them.

5.13.2.en: Some of the Fathers see that the wicked descend from sin to sin as if they were making a long rope that draws them toward evil in bondage... Every fall leads to another fall and every descent causes a further descent, so that instead of the wicked man thinking of ascending, he collapses more and more.

5.13.3.en: * Truly, every man weaves a rope for himself with his sins: “Woe unto them that draw iniquity as with a long rope” [18 LXX].

5.13.4.en: Who makes a long rope? He who adds sin to sin.

5.13.5.en: How is sin added to sin? When we cover a sin that was committed with another sin.

5.13.6.en: * When (the wicked) threaten to kill the righteous, they only bind themselves with chains, with a strong, rough rope of their own making.

5.13.7.en: * Blessed are those who in work and conduct sing the songs of ascents (degrees), and woe to those who draw sin like a long rope (and so descend with it).

5.14.0.en: St. Augustine Besides the gravity of sin in that it draws a person into a chain of sins, making him like a ball with which sins play, the second danger is that it stirs up a spirit of contempt and mockery instead of the person's desire to be freed from it, so the wicked repeat: “Let him make speed, and hasten his work, that we may see it: and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw nigh and come, that we may know it!” [19]. They doubt the possibility of God's judgment, so they suppose that they are able to face Him with proofs and arguments. In contempt they repeat “the Holy One of Israel,” the title that the prophets used for their hope in the coming of the Messiah, the Savior... as though they were throwing this hope to the wind.

5.14.1.en: In every age there are wicked people who make light of God's long-suffering and mock His promises and His love, as well as His disciplines, thinking they are mere words or illusions that will not be fulfilled:

5.14.2.en: “Behold, they say unto me, Where is the word of the LORD? let it come now” (Jer 17:15).

5.14.3.en: “The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth” (Ezek 12:22).

5.14.4.en: “There shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, and saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation” (2 Pet 3:4).

5.15.0.en: D. “Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!” [20]. The fourth woe falls on those who confuse truth with falsehood, good with evil, light with darkness, sweetness with bitterness, knowledge with ignorance. These give sin a coating of virtue, as when they justify anger by defending the truth, or condemning others under the cover of the desire for reform, and so on...

5.15.1.en: St. Clement of Alexandria sees that this woe is a threat against liars and the proud. God is the Truth, and the devil is the liar and the father of liars; whoever knows the will of God knows the truth and walks in goodness, but whoever ignores the divine will leaves the circle of truth to live in falsehood, and in this he loses his ability to discern and perceive the good, or the light, or the true knowledge of heavenly and divine things.

5.16.0.en: E. The claim of wisdom and understanding together with contempt for the opinions and counsel of others: “Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!” [21].

5.16.1.en: * He who is occupied with his own self and does not seek the counsel of others bears the mark of folly. It is said: “Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him” (Prov 26:12).

5.17.0.en: St. John Chrysostom F. The mighty who corrupt their powers: “Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink” [22]. When leaders are occupied with feasts, luxury and drunkenness, they lose their true role; thus we often corrupt our own powers by our departure from our serious goal and our immersion in the pleasures of this world.

5.18.0.en: G. Taking bribes: “Which justify the wicked for reward, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!” [23].

5.19.0.en: 24 Therefore as the fire devoureth the stubble, and the flame consumeth the chaff, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust: because they have cast away the law of the LORD of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel. 25 Therefore is the anger of the LORD kindled against his people, and he hath stretched forth his hand against them, and hath smitten them: and the hills did tremble, and their carcases were torn in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

5.19.1.en: Because of the sins that the people committed, the anger of the Lord was kindled like a flame of fire that burns the stubble, to make them like dust [24]. He allowed them to be disciplined with great firmness until the hills trembled and their carcases lay in the streets. Here he means what befell the people of God during the violent Assyrian invasion.

5.20.0.en: In the midst of this flame he says: “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still” [25]; He is still full of love, awaiting man's return to Him!

5.21.0.en: 26 And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far, and will hiss unto them from the end of the earth: and, behold, they shall come with speed swiftly: 27 None shall be weary nor stumble among them; none shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken: 28 Whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses' hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind: 29 Their roaring shall be like a lion, they shall roar like young lions: yea, they shall roar, and lay hold of the prey, and shall carry it away safe, and none shall deliver it. 30 And in that day they shall roar against them like the roaring of the sea: and if one look unto the land, behold darkness and sorrow, and the light is darkened in the heavens thereof.

5.21.1.en: The prophet presents to us a terrible description of the army of Assyria in its invasion of the people of God. This description reveals the invasion of the human soul by the enemy of good, with violence, ferocity and perseverance, and at the same time it rebukes the slack believers; for the wicked, for the sake of temporal spoil, do not tire until they achieve their goal, while the children of God are slack in obtaining fellowship in eternal glory.

5.22.0.en: A. “None shall be weary” [27]. In spite of the length of the distance they cover and the difficulties that face them, they feel no weariness because of their strong desire to enjoy the spoil... while we believers often grow slack in our spiritual striving under the pretext of exhaustion or weariness.

5.22.1.en: B. “Nor stumble” [27] in spite of the roughness of the road; perhaps because God called them to discipline His people, He made the road easy for them. It was more fitting for us not to fear the roughness of the road, for as long as we are in the hand of our Christ, “the Way,” we never stumble.

5.22.2.en: C. “None shall slumber nor sleep” [27] for the sake of the temporal and evil goal set before them. Is it not fitting for us believers neither to slumber nor sleep, but to remain awake in spirit until we achieve the aim of our mission?!

5.22.3.en: D. “Neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken” [27], that is, earnest and braced for work. The Lord commanded us: “Let your loins be girded about” (Lk 12:35), that we may fulfill the Lord's service with strength.

5.23.0.en: E. “Whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses' hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind” [28]. They are ready with their weapons and equipment, so as to fight with strength and for a long time and with lightning speed, and thus achieve the goal. It is fitting for believers to prepare against the battle of the devil with the spiritual weapons of faith of which the Apostle Paul spoke at greater length (Eph 6).

5.24.0.en: F. “Their roaring shall be like a lion, they shall roar like young lions: yea, they shall roar, and lay hold of the prey, and shall carry it away safe, and none shall deliver it” [29]. They bear the image of their master the devil, who walks about as a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour (1 Pet 5:8). It was fitting for believers to be sober and vigilant, resisting this enemy, stedfast in the faith (1 Pet 5:8-9), which is able to shatter the enemy.

5.24.1.en: The Lamb, the Lord of glory Jesus, came forward as a lion from the tribe of Judah (Rev 5:5), so that the devil may not defeat us, but we resist him by the Lord and shatter his powers.

5.25.0.en: G. “And in that day they shall roar against them like the roaring of the sea” [30], as the army falls upon them with the voices of the soldiers like the roaring of the sea that cannot be resisted, sweeping and swallowing all that is before it... as though they had no hope of escape from Assyria.

5.25.1.en: H. Finally the people lose all hope, for “if one look unto the land, behold darkness and sorrow, and the light is darkened in the heavens thereof” [30]. In the time of distress they lift up their eyes, perhaps to find a way of salvation, but darkness settles over their thoughts, and the clouds of smoke rising from the fires destroy every hope they have. They rejected God, “the true Light,” so darkness reigned in their depths. Therefore the psalmist cries: “In thy light shall we see light” (Ps 36:9).
